related_questions.question: Can having COVID cause blood clots?
related_questions.snippet: How does COVID-19 affect the blood? Some people with COVID-19 develop abnormal blood clots, including in the smallest blood vessels. The clots may also form in multiple places in the body, including in the lungs. This unusual clotting may cause different complications, including organ damage, heart attack and stroke.

related_questions.question: What is the difference between thrombosis and embolism?

text_blocks.snippet: Thrombosis and embolism are both conditions related to blood clots, but they differ in their formation and progression. Thrombosis is the formation of a blood clot (thrombus) within a blood vessel, while embolism refers to a clot or other substance that travels through the bloodstream and blocks a blood vessel. In essence, a thrombus can become an embolus if it detaches and travels.
snippet_highlighted_words: Thrombosis is the formation of a blood clot (thrombus) within a blood vessel, while embolism refers to a clot or other substance that travels through the bloodstream and blocks a blood vessel

list.snippet: Definition: Thrombosis is the process of a blood clot forming within a blood vessel.
Location: It occurs at the site where the clot forms.
Examples: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in a leg vein, arterial thrombosis in an artery.
Progression: A thrombus can remain stationary, or it can break loose and travel through the bloodstream.

list.title: Definition:
list.snippet: Embolism is the obstruction of a blood vessel by an embolus, which is a detached thrombus or other substance (like a fat globule or air bubble).

list.title: Location:
list.snippet: The blockage occurs at a location distant from where the embolus originated.

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: Pulmonary embolism (PE) when a clot from a DVT travels to the lungs, stroke when an embolus blocks a brain artery.

list.title: Progression:
list.snippet: Embolism is a consequence of a thrombus breaking loose and traveling.
